data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 defends the expert on the grounds that checklists are too coarse to capture non-linear interactions, but its own counterconditions concede entire task classes where this defense collapses (highly algorithmic tasks lacking complex non-linear dependencies; experts suffering cognitive decay). The problem asks the arguer to identify evidence within a single evaluation that distinguishes genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance tracking right answers. SRC_001 never supplies that evidentiary discriminator; it only asserts that panel 'coverage' is illusory on interaction-dependent outcomes, leaving no within-evaluation test for when checklist success is genuine vs. coincidental. Thus it answers the advocacy half while omitting the distinguishing-evidence half the problem requires.
